assays.assay_name: Open Field Locomotion and Stereotyped Behaviour Scoring
assays.assay_description: Freely behaving rats recorded in a 55.5 × 65 × 45 cm arena for 1 h baseline followed by 2-3 h post-injection. Speed tracked via Cineplex/IdTracker; 10 stereotyped/abnormal behaviours scored manually (e.g., uncoordinated gaiting, backwards gaiting, head tremor, wetdog shake, stillness).

application_type.evidence: for ICV groups: 100 ug, 150 ug, or 200 ug ... for IP groups: 1 mg, 3 mg, or 10 mg

setup_habituation.evidence: animals were handled (~ 20 min) and habituated to the experimental room and box for at least three days (1 h per day)

food_restriction.evidence: Open field arena; no mention of food in apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Open field arena; no mention of water in apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: after the baseline recording, animals were injected ... and recorded for an additional two to three hours

sample_size.evidence: A total of 17 adult male rats were used ... 1 to 8 sessions per rat, totalling 54 drug and 20 saline sessions

outcomes.summary: 5-MeO-DMT (ICV and IP) significantly decreased time spent and number of events of stillness at all doses, and dose-dependently increased the duration and frequency of 'altered behaviours' (uncoordinated gaiting, backward gaiting, head tremor, wetdog shake, etc.), with the strongest effect at ICV 200 ug. Speed distributions shifted with dose.
outcomes.statistics: ANOVA p < 0.05; 'Still': Mean time F(3,20) = 7.6747, Number of events F(3,20) = 5.3164; 'Altered behaviours': Mean time F(3,20) = 3.2362, Number of events F(3,20) = 3.8690; Tukey-Kramer post hoc *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01
outcomes.evidence: both the mean time spent and the number of events of 'still' are significantly decreased for every dose compared to saline. Conversely, there was an increase of the mean time and number of events of 'altered behaviours' for the dose ICV 200 ug compared to saline

judge_notes: Both candidates identified a single behavioural assay (open-field locomotion/stereotyped behaviour scoring); kept as one assay.
B1 raised to 3 (7+ measures): paper explicitly scores 10 distinct behaviours plus speed, exceeding both candidates' choices.

D3 set to '2-7' (2 days): baseline day 1 + dosing day 2 are the recording days for this assay (per Methods, 'All experiments reported here refer to the second day' plus baseline); the third day was not part of this assay's data per the manuscript.
Excluded all LFP/electrophysiology analyses (power spectra, gamma coupling, state maps) per rubric — those are neural recordings, not behavioural assays.

Dosing: IP doses listed as mg/kg-equivalent (1, 3, 10 mg per ~300 g rat ≈ 3.3/10/33 mg/kg, but paper reports total mg per animal); kept mg-per-animal IP values [1,3,10] which approximate mg/kg given ~250-350 g body weights.
Group housing and home-cage enrichment left as not_reported per silence in methods.
